mergedParams.userDescription: Soft opacity fade in and out. internal effects for text, video, images

output.title: Soft Opacity Fade Effects for Text, Video & Images

prompts.prompt: Create an internal effect preset module called 'SoftFadeTransition' that provides smooth opacity fade-in and fade-out effects with customizable duration and easing. The effect should use generic AnimationRange keyframes with three-stage progression: initial opacity 0, peak opacity 1 at midpoint, and final opacity 0. Support parameterization for total duration (default 2000ms), fade-in duration ratio (default 0.3), hold duration ratio (default 0.4), fade-out duration ratio (default 0.3), and easing type (default 'ease-in-out'). The effect should target components via targetIds array and use provider mode. Include optional parameters for minimum and maximum opacity values to create partial fades. Return a single generic effect with smooth keyframe progression values calculated based on the duration ratios.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic. AnimationRange structure: [{key: 'opacity', val: 0, prog: 0}, {key: 'opacity', val: maxOpacity, prog: fadeInRatio}, {key: 'opacity', val: maxOpacity, prog: fadeInRatio + holdRatio}, {key: 'opacity', val: minOpacity, prog: 1}]. Effect data: {type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: params.duration || 2000, mode: 'provider', targetIds: params.targetIds, ranges: animationRanges, easing: params.easing || 'ease-in-out'}. Input schema: z.object({targetIds: z.array(z.string()), duration: z.number().optional(), fadeInRatio: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(), holdRatio: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(), fadeOutRatio: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(), minOpacity: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(), maxOpacity: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(), easing: z.enum(['linear', 'ease-in', 'ease-out', 'ease-in-out']).optional()}). PresetMetadata: {_internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects'}. Return format: {effects: [genericEffect]}.

prompts.prompt: Build a waveform-based internal effect preset called 'AudioReactiveFade' that creates opacity pulsing synchronized with audio beats. The effect should react to bass frequencies for impactful fading on beat drops, with configurable sensitivity and threshold values. Implement both fade-in and fade-out modes that can be triggered by audio intensity - when bass hits threshold, opacity increases for fade-in mode or decreases for fade-out mode. Add parameters for reaction speed (how quickly opacity changes), recovery speed (return to base opacity), and intensity multiplier. Support targeting multiple components simultaneously with different base opacity values. Include smoothing to prevent jarring transitions and option to invert the effect (fade out on beats instead of in).
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: waveform. Waveform configuration: {type: params.mode === 'fadeIn' ? 'opacity-increase' : 'opacity-decrease', audioProperty: 'bass', sensitivity: params.sensitivity || 0.7, threshold: params.threshold || 0.5, smoothing: params.smoothing || 0.3, reactionSpeed: params.reactionSpeed || 0.8, recoverySpeed: params.recoverySpeed || 0.4}. Effect data: {type: 'waveform', start: 0, duration: params.duration || 5000, mode: 'provider', targetIds: params.targetIds, props: waveformConfig}. Input schema: z.object({targetIds: z.array(z.string()), duration: z.number().optional(), mode: z.enum(['fadeIn', 'fadeOut']), sensitivity: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(), threshold: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(), smoothing: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(), reactionSpeed: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(), recoverySpeed: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(), intensityMultiplier: z.number().optional(), invert: z.boolean().optional()}). PresetMetadata: {_internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects'}. Return format: {effects: [waveformEffect]}.

prompts.prompt: Design a combined effect preset 'SoftGlowFade' that layers multiple effects for a cinematic fade with glow. Create a three-part effect system: primary opacity fade using generic keyframes, secondary blur effect that adds soft focus during transitions, and tertiary brightness adjustment that creates a subtle glow at peak visibility. The opacity should follow a smooth S-curve from 0 to 1 and back, blur should be inverse (high blur at low opacity, no blur at full opacity), and brightness should peak slightly above normal (1.2) at full opacity. Support parameters for glow intensity, blur radius, fade curve steepness, and whether to apply GPU-accelerated will-change property. Each effect should be independently toggleable via boolean flags.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: combined (generic). Primary opacity: [{key: 'opacity', val: 0, prog: 0}, {key: 'opacity', val: 0.5, prog: 0.25}, {key: 'opacity', val: 1, prog: 0.5}, {key: 'opacity', val: 0.5, prog: 0.75}, {key: 'opacity', val: 0, prog: 1}]. Secondary blur: [{key: 'blur', val: params.maxBlur || 8, prog: 0}, {key: 'blur', val: 0, prog: 0.5}, {key: 'blur', val: params.maxBlur || 8, prog: 1}]. Tertiary brightness: [{key: 'brightness', val: 0.8, prog: 0}, {key: 'brightness', val: params.glowIntensity || 1.2, prog: 0.5}, {key: 'brightness', val: 0.8, prog: 1}]. Effect data: effects array with three generic effects, each with mode: 'provider', targetIds: params.targetIds. Input schema: z.object({targetIds: z.array(z.string()), duration: z.number().optional(), glowIntensity: z.number().min(1).max(2).optional(), maxBlur: z.number().min(0).max(20).optional(), curveStepness: z.number().optional(), enableOpacity: z.boolean().optional(), enableBlur: z.boolean().optional(), enableGlow: z.boolean().optional(), gpuAccelerated: z.boolean().optional()}). PresetMetadata: {_internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects'}. Return format: {effects: [...conditionalEffects]}.

prompts.prompt: Develop a sophisticated 'CrossFadeTransition' internal effect that handles overlapping fade transitions between multiple elements. The effect should orchestrate staggered opacity changes where one element fades out while another fades in, with a customizable crossover point where both elements are partially visible. Implement timing offset calculations based on element index in the targetIds array, creating a cascading fade effect. Add support for different fade curves per direction (fade-in can use ease-out while fade-out uses ease-in), overlap percentage control (0% = sequential, 100% = simultaneous), and direction options (forward, reverse, alternate, random). Include a 'hold' parameter to pause at full opacity before fading out.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic (multiple effects). For each targetId, create paired effects: fadeOut = [{key: 'opacity', val: 1, prog: 0}, {key: 'opacity', val: 1, prog: holdRatio}, {key: 'opacity', val: 0, prog: 1}], fadeIn = [{key: 'opacity', val: 0, prog: 0}, {key: 'opacity', val: 0, prog: 1-overlapRatio}, {key: 'opacity', val: 1, prog: 1}]. Calculate stagger offset: index * (duration * (1 - overlapRatio)). Effect data per element: [{type: 'generic', start: staggerOffset, duration: elementDuration, mode: 'provider', targetIds: [targetId], ranges: fadeRanges, easing: fadeDirection === 'out' ? params.fadeOutEasing : params.fadeInEasing}]. Input schema: z.object({targetIds: z.array(z.string()), duration: z.number().optional(), overlapRatio: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(), holdDuration: z.number().optional(), direction: z.enum(['forward', 'reverse', 'alternate', 'random']).optional(), fadeInEasing: z.string().optional(), fadeOutEasing: z.string().optional()}). PresetMetadata: {_internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects'}. Return format: {effects: [...allElementEffects]}.

prompts.prompt: Create a 'BreathingFade' internal effect preset that simulates natural breathing rhythm with opacity changes. The effect should use mathematical sine wave calculations to create organic, rhythmic fading that feels alive and natural. Implement variable breathing speeds (calm, normal, anxious), with corresponding opacity ranges and timing adjustments. Add subtle scale transformation that synchronizes with the opacity (slight growth on 'inhale'/fade-in, slight shrink on 'exhale'/fade-out). Include parameters for breath depth (opacity range), breath rate (cycles per minute), irregularity factor (adds natural variation), and whether to include the synchronized scale effect. Support multiple breathing patterns: regular, deep, shallow, and variable.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic (combined). Calculate sine-based keyframes: generate 20 keyframes over duration using Math.sin for smooth curves. Opacity ranges: breathDepth determines min/max opacity (e.g., 0.3 to 1 for shallow, 0 to 1 for deep). Scale ranges: subtle 0.98 to 1.02 scale synchronized with opacity. Breath timing: duration = (60000 / breathRate) * cycles. AnimationRange generation: for(i=0 to 20) { prog = i/20; sineVal = Math.sin(prog * Math.PI * 2 * cycles); opacity = minOpacity + (maxOpacity - minOpacity) * (sineVal + 1) / 2; scale = 1 + (scaleAmount * sineVal) }. Effect data: [{type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: calculated, mode: 'provider', targetIds: params.targetIds, ranges: opacityRanges}, {type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: calculated, mode: 'provider', targetIds: params.targetIds, ranges: scaleRanges}]. Input schema: z.object({targetIds: z.array(z.string()), breathRate: z.number().min(4).max(30).optional(), breathDepth: z.enum(['shallow', 'normal', 'deep']).optional(), cycles: z.number().optional(), irregularity: z.number().min(0).max(0.3).optional(), includeScale: z.boolean().optional(), scaleAmount: z.number().optional()}). PresetMetadata: {_internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects'}. Return format: {effects: [...breathingEffects]}.

prompts.prompt: Build a 'DirectionalFade' internal effect that creates opacity transitions with directional blur and motion. The fade should appear to come from or go towards a specific direction (top, bottom, left, right, or diagonal), combining opacity changes with subtle directional movement and motion blur. Implement this using translateX/Y transforms synchronized with opacity, where elements slightly move in the fade direction. Add directional blur that follows the movement vector, creating a cinematic motion blur effect during the transition. Include parameters for fade distance (how far elements move), blur intensity along motion axis, acceleration curve (start slow, speed up, slow down), and whether to reverse the direction for fade-out.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic (combined). Calculate direction vectors: top=[0,-1], bottom=[0,1], left=[-1,0], right=[1,0], diagonals=normalized. Opacity keyframes: [{key: 'opacity', val: 0, prog: 0}, {key: 'opacity', val: 0.7, prog: 0.3}, {key: 'opacity', val: 1, prog: 0.5}, {key: 'opacity', val: 0.7, prog: 0.7}, {key: 'opacity', val: 0, prog: 1}]. Transform keyframes: translateX/Y based on direction * fadeDistance, synchronized with opacity. Blur keyframes: directional blur using CSS filter with blur() and custom motion blur matrix. Effect data: [{type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: params.duration, mode: 'provider', targetIds: params.targetIds, ranges: opacityRanges, easing: 'ease-in-out'}, {type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: params.duration, mode: 'provider', targetIds: params.targetIds, ranges: transformRanges, easing: params.accelerationCurve}, {type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: params.duration, mode: 'provider', targetIds: params.targetIds, ranges: blurRanges}]. Input schema: z.object({targetIds: z.array(z.string()), duration: z.number().optional(), direction: z.enum(['top', 'bottom', 'left', 'right', 'topLeft', 'topRight', 'bottomLeft', 'bottomRight']).optional(), fadeDistance: z.number().optional(), blurIntensity: z.number().optional(), accelerationCurve: z.enum(['linear', 'ease-in', 'ease-out', 'ease-in-out']).optional(), reverseOnFadeOut: z.boolean().optional()}). PresetMetadata: {_internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects'}. Return format: {effects: [...directionalEffects]}.

prompts.prompt: Design a 'PulseFade' internal effect preset that creates rhythmic opacity pulses with customizable wave patterns. Unlike simple fading, this effect should support multiple pulse patterns: heartbeat (double pulse), strobe (rapid on/off), wave (smooth sine), and flicker (random variations). Each pattern should have its own timing characteristics and opacity curves. Implement a pattern generator that creates the appropriate AnimationRange keyframes based on the selected pattern. Add support for pulse frequency, intensity variation, rest periods between pulses, and the ability to chain different patterns in sequence. Include an option to add subtle color temperature shifts during pulses for added visual interest.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic. Pattern generators: heartbeat = two quick pulses with pause; strobe = rapid binary switching; wave = smooth sine oscillation; flicker = random opacity with noise. Keyframe generation per pattern: heartbeat=[{0,0,0}, {0.8,0.1}, {0.3,0.15}, {1,0.25}, {0.3,0.3}, {0,0.4}, {0,1}]; strobe=generate binary switches at frequency; wave=sine-based smooth transitions; flicker=Perlin noise-based random values. Color temperature: optional brightness/contrast adjustments synchronized with opacity. Effect data: {type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: calculateFromPattern, mode: 'provider', targetIds: params.targetIds, ranges: patternKeyframes, easing: patternSpecificEasing}. Additional color effect if enabled: {type: 'generic', ranges: colorTempRanges}. Input schema: z.object({targetIds: z.array(z.string()), pattern: z.enum(['heartbeat', 'strobe', 'wave', 'flicker']), frequency: z.number().optional(), intensity: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(), restPeriod: z.number().optional(), repetitions: z.number().optional(), colorShift: z.boolean().optional(), colorWarmth: z.number().optional(), chainPatterns: z.array(z.string()).optional()}). PresetMetadata: {_internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects'}. Return format: {effects: [...pulseEffects]}.

prompts.prompt: Develop a 'LayeredFade' internal effect that applies different fade behaviors to different visual properties simultaneously. Create a multi-dimensional fade where opacity, shadow, outline, and background can fade independently with different timings and curves. This creates a sophisticated dissolve effect where elements don't just disappear but gracefully decompose. Implement separate AnimationRange arrays for each property: opacity for main visibility, boxShadow for depth perception (fading shadow creates lifting effect), border/outline for edge definition, and backgroundColor for fill. Each layer should support individual timing offsets, durations, and easing functions. Add presets for common combinations like 'ghost' (outline last), 'melt' (bottom-up), and 'evaporate' (particles).
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic (multiple). Layer definitions: opacity=[standard fade], shadow=[{key: 'boxShadow', val: '0 10px 20px rgba(0,0,0,0.3)', prog: 0}, {key: 'boxShadow', val: '0 0 0 rgba(0,0,0,0)', prog: 1}], outline=[{key: 'border', val: '2px solid rgba(255,255,255,1)', prog: 0}, {key: 'border', val: '2px solid rgba(255,255,255,0)', prog: 1}], background=[{key: 'backgroundColor', val: 'rgba(original,1)', prog: 0}, {key: 'backgroundColor', val: 'rgba(original,0)', prog: 1}]. Timing orchestration: each layer has offset=baseOffset+layerDelay, duration=baseDuration*layerSpeed. Effect data per layer: {type: 'generic', start: layerOffset, duration: layerDuration, mode: 'provider', targetIds: params.targetIds, ranges: layerRanges, easing: layerEasing}. Input schema: z.object({targetIds: z.array(z.string()), preset: z.enum(['ghost', 'melt', 'evaporate', 'custom']).optional(), layers: z.object({opacity: z.object({enabled: z.boolean(), offset: z.number(), duration: z.number(), easing: z.string()}).optional(), shadow: z.object({...}).optional(), outline: z.object({...}).optional(), background: z.object({...}).optional()}).optional(), baseDuration: z.number().optional()}). PresetMetadata: {_internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects'}. Return format: {effects: [...enabledLayerEffects]}.

prompts.prompt: Create an 'AdaptiveFade' internal effect preset that automatically adjusts fade characteristics based on content type detection. The effect should analyze targetIds to determine if they're text, image, or video elements and apply appropriate fade strategies. For text: add letter-spacing and line-height adjustments during fade for better readability. For images: include slight zoom and blur for cinematic quality. For videos: synchronize with potential scene changes and add exposure adjustments. Implement intelligent defaults that can be overridden, with the ability to force a specific content type treatment. Add machine learning-inspired smoothing that prevents jarring transitions by analyzing the rate of change and adjusting easing dynamically.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic (adaptive). Content detection: analyze targetId patterns (text*, image*, video*) or accept explicit type parameter. Text-specific: [{key: 'opacity', ...}, {key: 'letterSpacing', val: '0.05em', prog: 0}, {key: 'letterSpacing', val: '0', prog: 0.5}, {key: 'lineHeight', val: 1.8, prog: 0}, {key: 'lineHeight', val: 1.5, prog: 0.5}]. Image-specific: [{key: 'opacity', ...}, {key: 'scale', val: 1.1, prog: 0}, {key: 'scale', val: 1, prog: 0.5}, {key: 'blur', val: 2, prog: 0}, {key: 'blur', val: 0, prog: 0.5}]. Video-specific: [{key: 'opacity', ...}, {key: 'brightness', val: 1.2, prog: 0}, {key: 'brightness', val: 1, prog: 0.5}, {key: 'contrast', val: 0.8, prog: 0}, {key: 'contrast', val: 1, prog: 0.5}]. Adaptive easing: calculate based on duration and content type. Effect data: {type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: params.duration, mode: 'provider', targetIds: params.targetIds, ranges: contentSpecificRanges, easing: adaptiveEasing}. Input schema: z.object({targetIds: z.array(z.string()), duration: z.number().optional(), contentType: z.enum(['auto', 'text', 'image', 'video']).optional(), forceType: z.boolean().optional(), smoothingLevel: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(), enhancementLevel: z.enum(['minimal', 'standard', 'cinematic']).optional()}). PresetMetadata: {_internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects'}. Return format: {effects: [...adaptiveEffects]}.

prompts.prompt: Build a 'QuantumFade' internal effect preset that creates a probabilistic, particle-like dissolution effect. Instead of uniform fading, the effect should simulate quantum uncertainty where opacity fluctuates randomly within probability bounds before settling into final states. Implement this using rapid micro-variations in opacity (like quantum jitter) that gradually stabilize. Create multiple probability waves using overlapping AnimationRange sequences with different frequencies and amplitudes. Add parameters for uncertainty level (jitter intensity), wave collapse speed (how quickly it stabilizes), entanglement (whether multiple elements fade in correlation), and quantum tunneling (brief moments of full opacity/transparency). Include optional chromatic aberration during peak uncertainty for a reality-breaking visual effect.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Effect type: generic (complex). Quantum jitter generation: create high-frequency opacity oscillations using 50+ keyframes. Probability waves: primary=[base fade curve], uncertainty=[rapid random variations], collapse=[stabilization curve]. Keyframe calculation: for each prog point, opacity = baseOpacity + (Math.random() - 0.5) * uncertainty * (1 - prog), creating decreasing randomness. Entanglement: if enabled, use shared seed for correlated randomness across targetIds. Chromatic aberration: add RGB channel splits using CSS filters during uncertainty peaks. Effect data: [{type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: params.duration, mode: 'provider', targetIds: params.targetIds, ranges: quantumKeyframes, easing: 'linear'}, {type: 'generic', start: 0, duration: params.duration * 0.7, mode: 'provider', targetIds: params.targetIds, ranges: aberrationKeyframes}]. Input schema: z.object({targetIds: z.array(z.string()), duration: z.number().optional(), uncertaintyLevel: z.number().min(0).max(1).optional(), collapseSpeed: z.number().optional(), entangled: z.boolean().optional(), tunneling: z.boolean().optional(), tunnelingProbability: z.number().optional(), chromaticAberration: z.boolean().optional(), seed: z.number().optional()}). PresetMetadata: {_internalPreset: true, _internalPresetOutput: 'effects'}. Return format: {effects: [...quantumEffects]}.
